subject: Contingency credits, mitigation timeline, and path to a premium tier
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@pulsepay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@pulsepay.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Increased latency impact and request for remediation credits

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this — over the last two weeks we've seen repeated P95 latency spikes on the /generate endpoint that directly affected customer-facing payments flows. We ran a short walk-through with our engineering team and traced it to tail latency on longer contexts.

PulsePay is approaching renewal in August and we need clarity on three things before we commit to an expansion: 1) a mitigation timeline so we can plan our cutover, 2) whether Redwood will provide a retroactive credit for the recurring degraded performance in April/May, and 3) what the gating criteria and pricing delta would be to move to the premium SLO tier you mentioned in the RFP.

I've attached our incident notes and a couple of request items (redwood_incident_summary_may12-17.pdf). Can we get a proposal and an ask for a short call tomorrow (Wed) morning PT?

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Reliability
PulsePay

Elena, Monica — quick commercial note while Laura builds the technical plan:

We recognize the operational impact and historically offer two levers in these cases:
1) A retrospective service credit tied to the SLA shortfall for the impacted billing period(s). Typical crediting is prorated % of that month’s invoice or a fixed credit depending on the root cause classification.
2) A contractual amendment that upgrades PulsePay to our premium SLO tier (higher uptime and tighter P95 targets) with either reserved capacity or dedicated routing. That comes with a different pricing profile and a 30-day notice for reserved capacity allocation.

Because you're also evaluating expansion, I'd propose a blended approach: a one-time retroactive credit for April/May, plus a programmatic escalation into premium tier with a 60-day pilot discount to validate the improvements before the renewal term kicks in.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet with credit scenarios after the call and can convert RFI items into a tracked amendment (DocuSign-ready) if we align on terms.

—Rishi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Increased latency impact and request for remediation credits — technical plan

Elena — follow-up from our triage: great meeting this morning; summary and next steps below.

Summary of root cause: intermittent tail latency stemming from a combination of long-context KV cache churn and a recent kernel selection fallback for a small subset of models. Impact concentrated on requests >512 tokens during peak windows.

Proposed immediate mitigations (72h):
- Apply a targeted KV cache size bump for PulsePay tenant routing to reduce churn (deploy 48h).
- Enable aggressive small-batch fastpath (applies to <2048 token requests) for your routing policy (deploy 24–36h).
- Add a temporary routing rule to prefer lower-latency model variant for contexts >2048 when under sustained load (deploy 72h).

Pilot & premium tier proposal (60-day pilot):
- SLA target for pilot: 99.95% uptime; P95 <= 480ms for <=512 tokens, P95 <= 820ms for 512–2048, P95 <= 1200ms for >2048.
- Automatic fallback policy: model fallback enabled with a soft degrade (best-effort responses with reduced max tokens) rather than queueing when load crosses threshold.
- Measurement: We will publish token-level latency histograms and per-route SLO dashboards in the Console for PulsePay.

Commercial credit proposal (options):
A) Fixed credit: one-time credit equal to 15% of April+May invoices (applied to June invoice).
B) Prorated SLA credit: credit tied to observed SLA shortfall in April/May up to a cap of 20% of the two-month spend.
C) Blended: 10% fixed credit + 30-day pilot discount (50% off pilot incremental cost).

Next steps: Laura to push the KV cache and fastpath changes over the next 48 hours (we'll send a deployment ETA), and Rishi/Monica to confirm which credit scenario you'd prefer; we'll convert to an amendment.

Laura Bennett
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
